newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania airline Tarom to undergo restructuring.
newsitem.headline: Romania airline Tarom to undergo restructuring.

text.p: Romania's Transport Minister announced plans on Monday for the rapid restructuring of the national airline Tarom, including the sale of outdated Soviet-made aircraft, layoffs and cooperation with foreign airlines.
Soviet-made Ilyushin-62, IL-18 and Tupolev-154 planes will be sold or taken out of service. Staff involved in their maintenance will be laid off or assigned new jobs, Traian Basescu told reporters.

Basescu said Tarom would continue to use eight ageing Antonov-24 on domestic routes along with two recently acquired Franco-Italian ATR aircraft. International routes are served by two A-310 Airbus planes, five Boeing 737s and six BAC 1-11 aircraft.

Basescu's announcement followed a pledge last week by the State Ownership Fund (FPS), Tarom's majority stockholder, to reshape the airline. FPS president Sorin Dimitriu said Tarom needed to cut jobs, withdraw ageing aircraft and improve efficiency.

The plan also includes striking cooperation accords with foreign airlines. Basescu said he hoped Tarom would be able to sign such an accord in London this week with representatives of Trans-World Airlines of the United States.
Improving passenger services was another target under the restructuring programme.

Tarom has laboured under huge debts in recent years, compounded by high fees to air traffic control and airport authorities. Mediafax said Tarom's internal debts amounted to 80 billion lei and external debts worth $15.5 million.

A restructuring plan to make Tarom competitive in east European markets was initiated in 1995. But it stalled under leftists who held power after the collapse of communism in 1989 until their election defeat last year.
